automations.field_help.balance_max_age_s: Maximum balance age: if the latest energy balance is older than this, it counts as stale and rules with an energy value condition do not trigger.
automations.field_help.cooldown_seconds: Cooldown: after triggering, the rule pauses this long before it may trigger again. At least 30 seconds for rules with a switching command.
automations.field_help.history_enabled: Save history: records the triggers of this rule so they appear here under “Show history”. With the switch off, the rule keeps checking but keeps no list.
automations.field_help.history_limit: How many of the latest triggers are kept per rule. Older ones drop out. Only applies to rules with “Save history” switched on in the rule editor below.
automations.field_help.history_persist: With the box ticked, the history survives a restart of the service (file in the device directory). Unticked, the service keeps recording and the interface still shows the history, but it is never written to disk.
automations.field_help.hold_seconds: Hold time: the condition must be met without interruption for this long before the rule triggers. At least 30 seconds for rules with a switching command.
automations.field_help.hysteresis: Hysteresis: the condition only counts as no longer met once the value has fallen back below the threshold by this amount. Prevents constant switching on and off close to the threshold.
automations.field_help.json_key: JSON key: if the payload is a JSON document, the value is read from this key.
automations.field_help.location: Location for the sun times, in decimal degrees (e.g. 52.52 and 13.405 for Berlin). It never leaves the device. The service calculates sunrise and sunset itself.
automations.field_help.offset: Offset: this amount is added after scaling. A negative value holds back a reserve, for example.
automations.field_help.payload: Payload: the content sent to the topic, typically ON or OFF for a switch.
automations.field_help.publish_allowed_p: If left empty, the dashboard allows exactly the command_topics of all currently known device entities when saving. Newly added devices or entities need another save. As soon as anything is entered here, only this list applies.
automations.field_help.retain: Retained: the broker keeps the message and delivers it to every new subscriber. Usually unwanted for switching commands.
automations.field_help.scale: Scaling: the balance value is multiplied by this factor before it is sent.
automations.field_help.settling_seconds: Settling window: after a restart, the service waits this long before the first rule may trigger. Right after the start the readings are still incomplete.
automations.field_help.tick_interval_s: Tick interval: how often the service checks all rules.
automations.field_help.topic: Topic: the MQTT address the message is published to.

tailscale.help.no_auth_key: No auth key needed: this assistant uses the interactive Tailscale sign-in, and the dashboard neither stores nor processes an access key.
tailscale.help.setup_account: Create an account and a tailnet on tailscale.com if you do not have one yet.
tailscale.help.setup_installation: Tailscale must already be installed and set up as a service on this target system. This assistant does not install anything. For the ARMv6 installation on this Pi, see the internal note knowhow/tailscale-setup.md.
tailscale.help.setup_login: To sign in, click the sign-in link that appears in step 2. It opens Tailscale's account sign-in (Google, Microsoft, GitHub or similar) in a new tab, on any device.
tailscale.help.title: Preparation and external dependencies
tailscale.status.title: Status
tailscale.step1.not_found: Tailscale was not found on this system or the service is not running. Install it manually, then check again.
tailscale.step1.title: 1. Check requirements
tailscale.step2.auth_url_label: Open to sign in and confirm with your Tailscale account:
tailscale.step2.help: This setup can briefly affect an existing connection to the workshop network if it runs over a route that the sign-in itself changes. Normally, your current access to the dashboard stays uninterrupted.
tailscale.step2.no_permission: Signing in needs the system_actions permission.
tailscale.step2.title: 2. Start sign-in
tailscale.step3.info: Active is plain device access via this system's Tailscale IP. Every other device in the tailnet reaches it directly via its Tailscale IP or the MagicDNS name.
tailscale.step3.note: Subnet router, exit node, tailscale serve and tailscale funnel are not part of this assistant yet and are planned for a later stage.
tailscale.step3.title: 3. Check result
